_doc: world/house-rules.md — v114 the fine-print layer: per-door house facts (structured policy fields a brain can read) + posted sign copy (the taped-up lines a camera can read). Doors only — keys equal anchor+street tier business ids exactly. All money figures are GAME DOLLARS; a card minimum is a policy number, not a menu price. Signs are conditions, never scripts — a house rule constrains how the room is used, never what anyone does.

pay.card_min: cards accepted over a posted minimum (pay_min, game dollars)

restroom.code: keypad or token — the code moves with the receipt
restroom.ask: a key on a big object, handed over the counter

wifi.open: open network, name on the wall
wifi.none: no wifi — a deliberate posture, not a gap

laptops.weekdays_only: no laptops weekends — the brunch crush needs the tables
laptops.counter_only: laptops at the counter rail only

dogs.patio: dogs on the sidewalk/park side only
dogs.service_only: service animals only (the legal default, posted where argued about)

outside_food.park_spill: park food tolerated at the outdoor tables only

linger.welcome: stay as long as you like — the room is the product
linger.rush_limit: posted limit during the rush window only
linger.move_along: counter service — no seats, no lingering posture

tab.regulars: house tab exists for known regulars (mirrors regulars.json tab rows)
tab.none: no tabs — settle at the register

rules.doors_only: doors keys == anchor+street tier business ids, exactly — offstage orgs and reserved names carry no house rules
rules.full_house: every door's house object carries every fact_key exactly once — a house with no policy still says so
rules.consistency: pay:card_min requires pay_min (game dollars) and a posted sign naming it; pay:cash_only requires a posted CASH sign; restroom:code requires a sign at restroom_door or register; wifi:receipt requires a sign pointing at the receipt; tab:regulars requires at least one tab row in regulars.json
rules.no_people: signs and facts never name cast or regulars — 'ask the counter' is the whole sentence
rules.no_scripts: a rule is a condition on the room (what the space permits/charges), never an instruction to a character
rules.money_policy_only: the only money figure allowed is pay_min — card minimums are policy, not prices; menu prices live in menus.json
rules.sign_tone: posted copy reads like a real taped sign — terse, slightly weary, occasionally funny; no legalese, no policy numbers
